lessons.title: Paktakon! (Riddles - Grade 1 vocabulary)
lessons.lesson:
Presentation: Lolo is the riddle-master (riddling is an elder’s game - culturally apt). “Paktakon!
Pamati sing maayo… kag pangitaa ang sabat SA ENGLISH!” Riddles are spoken in simple Hiligaynon;
the ANSWER is chosen and spoken in English - the translation act is the game itself.
THE SIX RIDDLES (full text; answers are all Grade 1 words):
1. “May apat ka tiil ako, nagataghol: aw aw! Ano ako?” → dog
2. “Nagakanta ako kon aga: tuktugaok! Ano ako?” → chicken
3. “Diri ka nagatuon kag nagabasa. Diin ako?” → school
4. “Nagalangoy ako sa tubig, wala ako tiil. Ano ako?” → fish
5. “Ginabuligan ko ang mga masakiton sa ospital. Sin-o ako?” → doctor
6. “Diri nagapuyo ang imo pamilya. Diin ako?” → house
Format per riddle: Lolo speaks it (a small picture-hint fades in after 5 seconds - the scaffold for
strugglers) → 3 English answer cards (picture + word) → tap → Lolo reacts: “Husto!” or a gentle
“Liwata!” + replay.

GRADE 3 - COMPLETE CONTENT PACK
Mobile-Based Hiligaynon-English Language Learning Application Level: Grade 3 (ages 8-9, emerging
readers) · 5 Units · 15 Lessons · Main character: KOKA THE FROG
Global rules (all Grade 3 lessons):
● Lesson length 8-10 min MAX, and no passive stretch longer than ~30 seconds: stories are
SHORT (6-7 sentences), split into pages of 1-2 sentences, with a question or interaction every
2 pages
● Sentences are ≤ 7 words, present tense, one clause each - the child READS them; tapping any
sentence plays its audio (support on demand, no longer automatic)
● One new component for the whole grade: StoryScreen - illustrated pages of {image + 1-2
sentences, tap-to-hear} with question pages interleaved
● Wrong answer on a story question = the story auto-returns to the answer page, highlights

lessons.title: “The Monkey and the Turtle” (Philippine folktale)
lessons.story:
Pre-story words: monkey (amo) · turtle (bao) · banana tree · share
FULL RETOLD TEXT (8 short sentences, 4 pages):
● Page 1: "Turtle finds a banana tree in the river. Monkey says, 'Let's share!'"
● Q1 - WHO: "Who finds the tree?" → tap Turtle
● Page 2: "'I take the top!' says Monkey. Turtle takes the bottom."
● Q2 - WHAT: "What does Monkey take?" → tap the leafy top (vs roots)
● Page 3: "Monkey's top dies. Turtle's bottom grows tall!"
● Q3 - WHY (the first WHY!): "Why does Turtle's part grow?" → tap the roots picture (vs
leaves) - Tudlo Guide whispers the hint if retried: "Ang gamot ang nagakuha sang tubig!"
● Page 4: "Now Turtle has many bananas. He shares them with his friends anyway!"
● MORAL PAGE: Tudlo Guide asks: "Ano ang leksyon?" → 2 spoken+written choices: "Share fairly." vs
"Bananas are yummy." (one real moral, one silly-literal - teaches the CATEGORY of moral by
contrast)
After-story: TileBuilder: "Turtle shares + his bananas" · voice-read Turtle's kind line.

Presentation: Detective Tudlo Guide models on a 4-sentence micro-mystery, thinking ALOUD:
"The plate is empty! The fish is gone. Look - paw prints! The cat sleeps with a happy
face."
Tudlo Guide: "WHO?... WHAT happened?... WHY do I think it's the cat? - ang paw prints kag ang happy
face!" (evidence-pointing modeled explicitly).
Practice - 3 micro-mysteries (FULL TEXTS), each followed by 3 questions; new mechanic: ANSWER,
THEN TAP YOUR CLUE (the evidence sentence or picture detail):
Mystery A - "Ang Nadula nga Saging":
"Tudlo Guide has three bananas. Now she has two! Monkey sits in the tree. He looks very full."
● Q: "How many bananas now?" → 2 · Q: "WHO took the banana?" → Monkey, then TAP THE
CLUE → "He looks very full." · Q: "WHERE is Monkey?" → tree
Mystery B - "Ang Basa nga Salog" (The Wet Floor):
"The floor is wet. The window is open. It rained this morning. Bantay is dry."
● Q: "WHAT is the problem?" → wet floor · Q: "WHY is the floor wet?" → rain through the
window, TAP THE CLUE → "The window is open." · Q: "Was it Bantay?" → No, TAP THE CLUE
→ "Bantay is dry."
Mystery C - "Ang Nagahibi nga Bata" (The Crying Baby):
"The baby cries and cries. Her bottle is empty. Nanay brings milk. Now the baby smiles."
● Q: "WHY does the baby cry?" → hungry/empty bottle, TAP THE CLUE · Q: "WHO helps?" →
Nanay · Q: "How does the baby feel at the end?" → happy

sleeps / he swims)
3. "Ana plants a seed. She waters it every day. What happens NEXT?" → (a flower grows / it
snows / a bus comes) EITHER right or wrong, Tudlo Guide celebrates the ACT of predicting
("Detective guess!") and shows the clue that pointed to the answer.

lessons.title: Context Clues + THE GRADE 3 / APP CAPSTONE
lessons.lesson:
CONTEXT CLUES (the graduation skill): Tudlo Guide meets 4 sentences, each with one unknown word; the
surrounding sentence gives the meaning away. Pattern per item: READ → GUESS from 3 picture
choices → the CLUE WORDS light up → confirm. FULL TEXTS:
1. "Bantay is very gutom - he eats and eats and eats!" → gutom = ? → hungry (clues: "eats and
eats")
2. "The night is very madulom - Tudlo Guide cannot see!" → dark (clue: "cannot see")
3. "Lola's soup is mainit - be careful, do not touch!" → hot (clues: "careful... do not touch")
4. "Juan is kapoy - he ran twenty laps! He wants to sleep." → tired (clues: "ran... wants to
sleep")
(Design note: the mystery words are HILIGAYNON words embedded in English sentences - the child
decodes meaning from ENGLISH context, then Tudlo Guide reveals the English word. This flips the app's usual
direction and mirrors real bilingual reading. If validators prefer invented words instead, swap them in
- the mechanic is unchanged.)
Tudlo Guide then says the line that is the whole app in one sentence: "Kon indi mo kilala ang word - BASAHA
ANG PALIBOT NIYA!" (If you don't know the word - read around it!)
THE GRADE 3 / APP CAPSTONE - "Ang Graduation ni Tudlo Guide!" A final SHORT story (8 sentences -
attention-span capped) told in stops across the whole map, with ~14 embedded items sampling
every Grade 3 skill. FULL STORY TEXT:
● Page 1: "Today is a big day. Tudlo Guide graduates!" → 2 number items: "How many friends come?"
(count 12) · "How much are the flowers?" (price tag: 15 pesos)
● Page 2: "First, the friends make the plaza pretty. Ana brings long green leaves. Juan brings
round red lanterns." → 2 describing taps + 1 sequence item (first/next/then cards)
● Page 3: "But the sky is dark! What happens next?" → 1 prediction (rain!) → "Teacher says:
'To the school!'" → 1 WH + evidence tap: "Why do they move?" → tap the clue sentence
● Page 4: "Lolo tells one last riddle. Lola reads one small poem." → 1 riddle (Grade 2 pouch,
scheduler-picked) + 1 rhyme-completion
● Page 5: "Tudlo Guide says: 'Salamat - THANK YOU, my friends!' Everyone is happy - not sad!" → 1
opposite tap + 1 context-clue word + 1 main-idea card ("Friends help each other" - just right!)
● FINALE: the child voice-reads the last line aloud: "Goodbye, and thank you!" (record →
playback → the whole map cheers)
First-attempt data here = the terminal assessment; with the Grade 1 and Grade 2 capstones you now
have THREE comparable instruments charting the entire learning arc (the spine of your evaluation
chapter).
